verified_title: GR-2: A Generative Video-Language-Action Model with Web-Scale Knowledge for Robot Manipulation
problem: Manipulation policies trained on limited action data generalize poorly across objects/scenes; human video offers temporal and semantic priors without compatible robot controls.
contribution: Scale GPT-style video generative pretraining to38million clips, then jointly fine-tune future multiview image generation and continuous action chunks through a conditional VAE. Demonstrate broad multitask manipulation and bin picking with a comparatively compact default policy.
algorithm: Frozen text encoder and VQGAN produce discrete language/image tokens; train autoregressive future image prediction, then add trainable robot-state embeddings and a cVAE chunk decoder. Robot fine-tuning generates images and actions together. Synthetic distractor/background augmentation uses object inpainting,SAM and video generation while preserving demonstrated motion. A separate trajectory optimizer and WBC convert Cartesian chunks into hardware joint tracking.
observations: Language, current/history images from static and wrist cameras, and EE position/orientation plus binary gripper state. Prediction examples compare imagined versus actual rollout, but no independent causal contact identification is shown.
actions: Cartesian action trajectories decoded by cVAE, then smoothed and converted to joint commands. The Kinova tracker runs200Hz; this is a separate low-level WBC rate, not evidence of200Hz model inference. Exact policy chunk horizon and latency NOT_EXTRACTED.
embodiment_and_data: KinovaGen3 7DoF withRobotiq2F85 andtwo RGB views. Default230M parameters/95M trainable, with scaling up to719M trainable. Web video pretraining38M clips/~50B tokens. Physical105 tasks cover8skills using~40000demos (~400/task), with a~5000-demo subset (~50/task). Bin picking separately uses94000 demonstrations of55seen objects and tests122total objects.
experiments: Multitask simple/distractor plus unseen background,kitchen environment andmanipulation conditions; data-augmentation and scarcity variants. Bin picking tests seen/unseen and cluttered seen/unseen object sets. CALVIN ABCD-to-D uses1000chains of5tasks; it includes D training data and must not be compared as identical to ABC-to-D zero-shot evaluation.
baselines: GR-1 is the main physical comparison; CALVIN includes RT-1,MT-ACT,HULC,RoboFlamingo,GR-1. Large-scale pretraining,augmentation and action-data changes accompany model differences; all gains cannot be uniquely attributed to one architectural component.

quantitative_result.physical: PDFpp7–8:97.7% on105tasks in simple setting,71.4%unseen backgrounds/71.7%unseen environments; augmented variant87.0%unseen environments.50-demo/task variant73.9%simple; reported unseen-manipulation55.8%. Exact physical rollout denominators NOT_EXTRACTED;105tasks is not a trial count.
quantitative_result.bin_picking: PDFp8/Fig9:mean79.0% versusGR-1 33.3% across four seen/unseen/clutter conditions after94000demos; exact evaluation n NOT_EXTRACTED.

limitations: Strong simple-setting results depend on substantial web and robot data. Physical evaluation denominators,confidence intervals and policy latency are absent from extracted evidence. Unseen objects remain a major failure source. WBC smoothing,collision/manipulability constraints and synthetic augmentation are part of reported behavior; the learned model alone is not the full deployed system. No bimanual cloth/sock task is quantitatively established.
code_and_license: No actual code/checkpoint release,revision or licenses audited; no execution. Dataset citations and a technical report do not establish reusable model rights.
hardware_adaptation: COMPARE compact cVAE action chunks with video-supervised features against officialACT at matched data budgets. The230M scale is more plausible for an NX experiment than14B WAMs, but there is no NX runtime qualification. Two-view calibration and Cartesian-to-joint mapping differ from Explorer. Do not import the paper's WBC or change existing controller settings.
